content:
**issue-535 landed on main: the Requirement 6 / #340 collision the textual merge hid**

**Context.** The #535 chain (PRs #547/#548/#549/#550, four stacked branches on a tracker branch that had no PR to main) was complete and green, but based at `eb8810d` — before #546 (#340) and #553/#554 merged. Landing it meant replaying its 15 commits onto current main, which is where the real finding surfaced.

**The finding: two merged-doctrine requirements that only collide in the blanket form.** #535's Requirement 6 shipped a test forbidding ANY non-test module from importing `governance/run-check.mjs` ("entry point, never a library"). #340 (merged as #546, AFTER the chain branched) makes `brain-check.mjs:27` import `runCheck` on purpose — brain:check and CI must be ONE implementation of one rule. `git merge-tree` reports the merge clean; the test suite reports it red. Textual mergeability said nothing about semantic mergeability, and each side was written blind to the other because both were in flight at once.

**Resolution, and why not the other one.** The property per-invocation resolution actually needs (workflow-auth.mjs, Requirement 3) is narrower than the ban: no OTHER WORKFLOW-INVOKED entry point may reach run-check.mjs, because such a step carries no SUBCOMMAND_PORT_REACH manifest of its own and the guard therefore resolves it by whole-file closure, inheriting every subcommand's port-reach at once. `brain-check.mjs` is a local developer verb invoked by no workflow, so it cannot cost any CI step its precision. Narrowing keeps both requirements; reverting #340's import would re-create the defect #340 exists to remove. The narrowed test goes red the day anything reaching run-check.mjs becomes a workflow step — which is exactly when the extraction has to happen.

**How the narrowing avoided becoming its own defect.** The set of workflow-invoked entry points is derived through workflow-auth's OWN extraction (new export `workflowEntryPoints`) and its OWN closure walk (`importClosure`, now exported) — a second copy of either would be #340 a third time. Not an allowlist of file paths: that is the shape of the guard #480 defeated. `importClosure` stops at `vcs/ci-context.mjs` (the D1 cut vertex), which would hide a path to run-check.mjs through it, so that gets its own direct canary instead of an assumption.

**Red-proof, run live, not reasoned.** Appended a real `import { runCheck } …` to `brain/scripts/vcs/actor-check.mjs` (a genuine workflow entry point), confirmed the edit landed by reading the file back, ran the suite: RED with the intended message. Reverted from a pre-mutation snapshot, confirmed clean, green. A synthetic-file mutation test pins the walk itself so the invariant cannot start passing by seeing nothing.

**Corrected premise carried forward from the chain's own record.** #535's table claimed four steps declared GH_TOKEN; `issue-link` had already been moved to VCS_TOKEN by #479 (commit `316575a`), so the swap covered three. Verified on `origin/main` before landing, not taken from the ticket.

**State on landing.** 3174 tests, 0 fail; `repo:check` and `brain:nav` green. Non-test changed lines ~381 against the lite budget, well inside it — the chain was split into four PRs against a 400-line-per-PR working limit, but the tests are in `ignoreList`, so the whole thing lands as one PR without a waiver. Deferred, deliberately and at the maintainer's instruction: #551 (T7b's third vacuous-pass route — arrow-form dispatch handlers; test-coverage only, no production defect).

**Generalizable.** When two branches are in flight against the same subsystem, "merges clean" is not the parallelisability test — the test is whether either side introduces a STANDING INVARIANT the other side violates. An invariant is a claim about the whole tree; a diff is a claim about a few files. #459's `filesOverlap` compares file claims and would have called these two disjoint (`brain-check.mjs` + `governance/run-check.mjs` vs `workflow-auth.mjs` + `governance.yml`) — it cannot see an invariant whose scope is "every file". That is a real limit of the parallelisation signal, worth naming where the signal is documented.
